thesis: Paymentus Holdings (NYSE: PAY; screen file lists the company as Paymentus Holdings, SEC ticker PAY). Q3 2026 10-Q filed 2026-11-03 (cover, statements, customer funds, concentration read; MD&A truncated) and 8-K 2026-11-02 with Ex 99.1 read. Q3 revenue 372.2M (+19.8%), gross profit 93.8M (+25.4%), contribution profit 118.5M (+20.6%), adjusted EBITDA 49.7M (+38.6%), margin 41.9% of contribution profit, transactions 219.0M (+20.1%). 9M revenue 1,091.4M (+26.0%). Guidance FY26 revenue 1,464M to 1,469M, contribution profit 466M to 468M, adjusted EBITDA 186M to 191M; Q4 revenue 373M to 378M. TTM (FY25 + 9M26 - 9M25): revenue 1,421.8M, gross profit 358.4M, NI 94.6M, OCF 168.1M, capex (PP&E plus capitalized software) 38.4M, FCF 129.7M, SBC 24.1M (FCF after SBC 105.6M). Shares 126,111,148 (78,633,959 Class A + 47,477,189 Class B, cover 2026-10-29) x 32.82 = market cap 4,139M = 43.8x TTM NI, FCF yield 3.1% (2.6% after SBC). Cash 407.6M, no debt line seen, total liabilities 120.6M; EV about 3,731M = 2.6x TTM revenue, 10.4x TTM gross profit. No customer above 10% of revenue. Close 32.82 on 11-17, down 4.1% from 34.22.
counterthesis: Price is 44x trailing earnings; revenue growth is high but gross margin is only about 25%, and the TTM FCF yield of 3.1% needs continued 20% growth. Quality of FCF is unconfirmed (working capital, settlement timing, funds in custodial accounts of 206.1M are off balance sheet). Revenue growth may include a large reseller or low-margin pass-through volume; one reseller exceeds 10% of receivables. Insider Form 4 filings on 11-17 and 13G/A amendments on 11-05 and 11-13 were seen in submissions but not read (could be sales). Founder control through Class B (47.5M shares, 38% of total) limits minority influence. Competitors (Fiserv, ACI, Bill, PayNearMe, Invoice-based processors) not compared. Cause of the 4.1% drop on 11-17 unknown; earlier run mention of an August acquisition could not be confirmed (8-K 2026-08-03 has no Item 2.01, goodwill flat).
invalidation: Thesis fails if growth in contribution profit slows below about 12%, adjusted EBITDA margin falls back below mid-30s, FCF conversion drops while revenue grows, or major biller or reseller losses appear.
